rows.en: "Aaaaaghh!"{p}

What stood before him was himself, rotted all the way through.
Himself, so changed he looked like a corpse that had crawled out of its grave.
You know what a doppelganger is?
It's your other self.
They say if you meet it, you'll die before long.{p}

...The next day, Tadokoro was found dead in the gym.
They say his face was frozen in terror, too hideous to look at twice.
In the end, they settled it as Tadokoro losing his mind and killing himself in the gym.
The cause of death is unknown.
Officially, they're calling it a heart attack.{p}

...That's the story they pass down in the basketball club.
How does anyone know it, if Tadokoro died, you ask?
Heh heh heh... What do you think happened to that notebook?
I hear it's still somewhere in the basketball club.
Though they say it's not easy to find, even if you go looking.
And what's more, there's a second volume.
Of course, as for who wrote the second one... you know, don't you?
And what was written in it, too.
The story goes that someone found it by chance and read it.
That's why this story keeps getting passed down.
You do sports, right?
I don't know what you play, but don't overdo it.{p}
...By the way, do you have an older brother?
Yes
No

Ask whether he's got some secret he's hiding.
And then, if your brother goes pale...
Heh heh, you'd better watch yourself too.
That's the end of my story.
Let's hear the next one.{p}

If you're thinking about starting a sport at this school... there's something I want to warn you about.
At our school, people who play sports have had all kinds of encounters with spirits.
There's a lot of dangerous stuff going on.
Sports are about pushing yourself to your limits, right?
It's an all-out, serious contest.
So the passion of people who play sports is something else.{p}

You know this?
When a person's will is strong, spirits are more likely to go after them.
There are spirits that slip into the cracks in your heart, like wanting to get stronger or wanting to beat somebody, and do their dirty work.
To avoid that, you need a heart strong enough to throw spirits off.
{a}, you'd better build up a heart like that too.
It'd be stupid to stay out of the sports clubs just because spirit stuff happens more there.{p}

Still, no matter how strong your heart is, there are plenty of ways to fall into a trap.
So on top of a strong heart, you need to keep your eyes open too...
Let me tell you about a certain athlete.
The boys' volleyball team at our school went away to summer training camp.
The camp lodge is one of our school's facilities.{p}

It's a building that came with some land the school bought, and they just use it as is.
It's up in the mountains, and apparently it used to be a school.
It's wooden, a shabby old building that looks like it could fall apart any minute.
But since it was a school, it's got a gym.
So the clubs use it a lot for training camps.{p}

...If you join a sports club, you might end up going there for camp too.
The roof leaks and the walls are covered in stains. It's seriously creepy.
And you lay out futons and sleep right there.
Maybe it's the perfect place for some sweat-and-guts sports drama.
But I hear things show up a lot when you go there for camp.
What shows up?
Spirits, obviously.
Everyone says you hear a woman crying, or moaning, or that there's a human-shaped stain on the wall.
So, about that boys' volleyball camp.
.........{p}

The camp ended without a hitch.
But when they got back to school, there was one more ball than before.
The first-year who was sorting the club's equipment noticed something was off.
But he thought it might just be his imagination, so he didn't tell anyone.
That's when it all started.{p}

Players started getting hurt, one after another, during practice.
At first it was just scrapes from falling, or twisted ankles.
But as time went on, there were accidents like torn Achilles tendons and broken bones.
That went on for about a month, and everyone started to think something was strange.
So the team members thought it over.
The injuries on the boys' volleyball team had started... right around when they... got back from camp.
Then one day, there was a practice match against another school.
They invited the volleyball team from a nearby high school to play at our school...{p}

After that, a first-year on the team started saying the ball was what was suspicious.
When they got back from camp, there'd been one extra ball.
Everyone scratched their heads, wondering if there had even been any balls at the camp lodge.
But if it was true, they decided they'd better do something about that ball.
Everyone figured that if it came from that lodge, it being cursed made perfect sense.
But the club had about twenty balls in storage.
There was no way to tell which one was the extra.
Still, they couldn't afford any more accidents.
So, just to be safe, they threw out every ball the boys' volleyball team had at the time.
Then they went and bought twenty brand-new balls.
And after that, the accidents at practice stopped dead.
Strange things happen, huh?
Everyone kept telling each other what a scary business that had been.
But then...
One day, about two weeks later, there was one extra ball in the club's stock again.
This time, they could tell exactly which one it was.{p}
Because among the newly bought balls, there was one single ball that was old and filthy.{p}That's right, the cursed ball had come back...
Have it exorcised
Throw the ball out again

They couldn't let there be any more victims.
That's what everyone thought, so they decided to have an exorcism done.
One of the members saw an ad tucked in the corner of a magazine and brought in an exorcist.
And the exorcist started saying something like this:
"This ball is possessed by the spirit of a student who died in an accident.
It seems he was on a volleyball team, and was hit by a car on his way to an important match.
It's better to perform the exorcism at night.
I'll come back here tonight, and I'd like one of you to come along with me then..."
So a first-year on the team ended up going with the exorcist.{p}

He was the one who'd first noticed there was an extra ball after camp.
His name was... Matsumoto, I think.
Matsumoto was the great hope of the boys' volleyball team.
He'd been playing volleyball since elementary school.
His father was a P.E. teacher, and apparently taught him all kinds of things.
He was tall, and his jumping ability was outstanding.
Plus, in middle school, he'd been on the team that won the Tokyo tournament.
Matsumoto had a good personality, too.
Nobody would want to go along to an exorcism at school at night, right?
But when it came up, he was the first to volunteer.
And so Matsumoto arranged to meet the exorcist at the school that night.{p}

It was a chilly day, right as autumn was setting in.
Matsumoto showed up about twenty minutes before the agreed time.
But the exorcist was already standing at the school gate.
"I've been waiting for you..."
The exorcist said that with a smile.
Seeing it, Matsumoto shuddered.
It should have been nothing but a polite smile, but he couldn't help finding the exorcist creepy.
He only felt that way because the school was scary at night.
That's what Matsumoto told himself.
The exorcism was to be held in the gym.{p}

The two of them crossed the schoolyard, one step at a time.
Heading for the gym, Matsumoto felt a chill creeping up his spine, colder and colder.
There wasn't any wind, yet it felt like something was passing across his back.
It felt like something cold was licking at him from behind. Swish... swish...
And then, when the two of them entered the gym...{p}

A ball was lying all alone on the floor.
It was that cursed ball.
At noon that day, they were sure they'd put the ball away in the gym storeroom.
So why was it here now...?

Matsumoto started shaking violently.
But he couldn't very well go home now.
"Well then, Matsumoto.
Let's begin the exorcism."
The exorcist was grinning.
Why was the exorcist grinning?
What was this person grinning about...?
"Matsumoto... I'm so happy.
To think you'd help someone like me.
Now, pick up the ball over there.
And hold it tight against your chest."{p}

Matsumoto did as the exorcist said.
Or rather, it felt like his body moved on its own.
Something was wrong with this exorcist.
Even thinking that, he couldn't resist.
"Now, pray while you hold the ball.
For the spirit of the athlete who never got his due.
Save him, with your pure heart that loves sports..."
Matsumoto prayed with all his might.
If he'd been killed in a car accident before a match, he might not be able to rest in peace either.
Matsumoto could feel that athlete's bitterness as clearly as if it were his own.{p}

"Ah... Matsumoto.
I'm so happy... thank you.
Thank you... You understand how I feel, don't you..."
Before long, the exorcist started saying things like that.
"More... pray more...
Then I can rest in peace... and the ball's curse will be lifted.
If I, if only I can rest in peace..."
The exorcist's form changed into a boy in a gym uniform, glowing a hazy white.
Matsumoto kept praying desperately.
"Thank you. Thank you.
Thank you..."
The boy in the gym uniform faded into the haze and vanished...
At the same moment, the ball in Matsumoto's hands vanished too.{p}

All that was left was Matsumoto, alone in the gym at night...
Do you get what that means?
The spirit of the athlete who'd cursed the ball had shown up disguised as the exorcist.
And he'd gotten Matsumoto to pray his soul to rest.
Apparently the real exorcist who'd taken the job got into a car accident and never made it.
The whole thing had been set up by the athlete's spirit.{p}

...Whoa, the story doesn't end there.
It's about Matsumoto.
The moment the athlete's spirit passed on, Matsumoto felt a violent pain in his legs and arms.
But there was no calling for help in the gym at night, and they say he writhed all alone on the cold floor.
Matsumoto couldn't stand.
The pain in his legs and arms was so bad he couldn't even crawl.
Before long, his eyes started to hurt too.
And then Matsumoto passed out...
The next day, Matsumoto was found collapsed.
The bones in his legs and arms were broken.
His ankles had been twisted, and his Achilles tendons were torn.
He was covered in bruises and wounds, and the surface of his eyes was scratched...
That's right. It was everything that had happened to the people the ball's curse had hurt.
All of it hit Matsumoto at once.
And the people hurt by the ball's curse all made a full recovery.
As the price for lifting the ball's curse, Matsumoto ended up sacrificing his own body...{p}

How about that, {a}?
Sports are great.
But if you go to this school, you've got to stay careful even during club practice.
Don't go sticking your nose into anything reckless.
Though I'd say this seven wonders interview of yours is already pretty death-defying.
That's as far as my story goes.
Want to hear the next one...?{p}

The ball rolled by itself across the schoolyard, all the way to the volleyball club room.
The club room door was shut at the time.
But the ball slipped right through the door and got inside.
Then it set the club room on fire, starting a small blaze.
The members scrambled to put it out.
Luckily, the fire went out quickly.
But...{p}

Black soot and scorch marks were left caked onto the charred club room wall.
And those scorch marks...
Were in the shape of a person.
They say the shape looked just like the stain on the wall at the camp lodge.
What shape do you think it was?{p}
...That's right, it was shaped like an athlete holding a ball.

Long ago, when that camp lodge was still a school, a volleyball player apparently died in an accident.
That spirit must have seen our school's camp and envied them.
It turned itself into a ball and followed everyone back.
It hurt everyone because it wanted them to notice it was there.{p}

And they did notice, all right.
But instead of laying the spirit to rest, they threw it into the incinerator...
Well, I'd say the spirit went about it the wrong way too.
In the end, that spirit held a grudge over how the team treated it and became an earthbound spirit.
Apparently that club still gets a lot of injuries even now.
.........{p}

Listen, {a}.
A strong heart and a watchful eye. That's what matters.
If you're going to start a sport, that is...
That's as far as my story goes.
Who's telling the next one...?{p}

I see...
Everyone who doesn't play sports gives that answer.
Like they're scrambling to cover it up.
Nobody's saying it's bad not to play sports.
Well, whatever.{p}

That's right.
Tadokoro got someone to take photos of him being beaten, and went to show them to a teacher.{p}

That's exactly it.
Tadokoro got someone to take photos of him being beaten, and went to show them to Kawaguchi.{p}

And he tried to talk Kawaguchi into quitting the track team and coming over to basketball.
But Kawaguchi figured the track seniors must have had some reason for doing this.
After all, the track seniors had always been kind to Kawaguchi.
Kawaguchi decided they'd done what was in those photos to keep their star safe from Tadokoro's clutches.
So this is what Kawaguchi told Tadokoro:
There was no way Kawaguchi was joining basketball.
But Tadokoro didn't give up.
After that, he kept coming around to see Kawaguchi, still pushing for the basketball team.{p}

You think so?
Kawaguchi had been doing track ever since middle school.{p}

Well, it seems that was true at first.
Kawaguchi's old man used to hold a sprint record back in the day.
Kawaguchi got into track because of the old man.
It seems it was grudging at first, but the kid had talent.
After setting record after record, Kawaguchi started taking sprinting seriously, the story goes.
So no matter how hard Tadokoro recruited, Kawaguchi's mind didn't change.{p}

Tadokoro talked to the team members.
He asked them to make him captain again.
But everyone kept their mouths shut and said nothing.
Tadokoro was so frustrated he couldn't stand it.
He loved basketball, loved it more than he could bear.{p}

Hey, {a}.
You know the word 'sportsmanship,' right?
You always hear it at the opening ceremonies of school sports days and track meets.
"We, the athletes, pledge to compete fair and square in the spirit of sportsmanship..."
The athletes' oath, they call it.
If anything sums up a true sportsman, it's those words.
Anyone who loves sports should face everything fair and square.{p}

Someone who pulls underhanded stuff like Tadokoro can't be called a sportsman.
The team members' resentment of Tadokoro grew even stronger...
And without anyone in particular starting it, they began ignoring Tadokoro.
By the time Tadokoro noticed, nobody around him would have anything to do with him.
He must not have liked that.
He turned into an even nastier piece of work.
And finally, he quit the basketball team.
Nobody objected.
If anything, I bet they were glad.
In basketball, teamwork matters more than anything.
Someone like Tadokoro, with skill but no team spirit, was nothing but dead weight.
And that dead weight was going away.
Everyone thought that would settle everything nicely.{p}

So, about Tadokoro after he quit the basketball team...
After quitting, I hear he secretly started a new club.{p}

He went around saying,
"We save talented students the world doesn't understand!"
or some such, but talk about a brat with a twisted grudge.
Teachers and the captains of the sports clubs warned him again and again, but Tadokoro's harassment just kept getting nastier.
It had no effect at all.
Well, if he'd been the type to quietly listen to warnings, it would never have come to this.
The school couldn't keep quiet about it anymore.
Tadokoro was going to be forced to transfer, right before graduation.
And he got furious.
"I'll never leave this school!"
He said that and ran out of the classroom, and he still hadn't come back by the end of the school day.{p}

What a pain that guy was, right to the very end.
You think so too, don't you?
And on top of that, Tadokoro kept causing nothing but trouble even after he died.
Haven't you ever noticed how many people in our sports clubs get hurt?
Sure, if you train hard, a couple of injuries might be only natural.
But there are way too many unnatural accidents.
Last year, a tennis player who won the singles title fell down the stairs the very next day and sprained an ankle.
That player swore,
"Somebody pushed me!"
and stuck to that story.
Even though there was nobody around.
There was also someone who got locked in the gym storeroom.
Even though... it doesn't even have a lock.{p}

Weird, right?
There are tons of incidents like that.
And they only ever target the aces of the sports clubs.
So, without anyone in particular starting it, people began saying the whole string of accidents and incidents was Tadokoro's doing.
"I had talent, and nobody understood me."
That's the grudge he takes out on the other aces, they say, by getting them hurt.{p}

{a}, you do sports, right?
I don't know what you play, but be careful.
If you're making too big a splash, Tadokoro will have his eye on you.
Well then, let's hear the next person's story...{p}

Close, but no.
What was written there was the story of someone a lot like Tadokoro.{p}

That's right. How to summon a demon.
The lined pages of the notebook were filled with basketball team data, training methods and so on.
But all over the margins, instructions for summoning a demon were scrawled.
Tadokoro turned the pages one by one, reading through how to perform the ritual.
Then he copied it all out onto a separate sheet of paper.
But there was one item missing.
You needed four ingredients to summon the demon.
A frog's heart, alcohol, laurel leaves, and...
One more.
What that last ingredient was, it didn't say.
Tadokoro searched every corner of the notebook.
Then he noticed that one page had been torn out and was missing.
The last ingredient must have been written on that page.
Along with how to summon the demon, the notebook also said this.{p}

"The demon summoned by this method has the power to erase people's memories.
Whose memories, and which ones, are decided by the one who performs the summoning ritual.
This demon belongs to a race that feeds on human memories."
Reading that, Tadokoro got to thinking.
If he could erase the memories of everyone on the basketball team, and Kawaguchi's...
Maybe he could wipe every bad memory of him out of their minds and become basketball captain again.
But summoning a demon has to be dangerous, right?
And he didn't even know the last ingredient.
So Tadokoro tried to give up on it.{p}

And then, guess what?
From somewhere, he heard a voice.
"Tadokoro, you read the notebook, didn't you..."
Tadokoro looked around.
But no one was there.
"It's all right.
You only need to gather three of the ritual ingredients.
I've already got my eye on the last one.
I've tried that ritual myself, you see..."{p}

Tadokoro's cheeks went stiff with nerves.
The voice went on.
"I used to be on this school's basketball team.
I want to help you.
Because you've got real passion for basketball.
I've really taken a liking to you for it.
Truth is, I got into trouble with the other members back then too, and I tried this method to make them forget it...
But I died in an accident before I could make my mark on the team.
It's so frustrating.
You love basketball, so you understand how I feel, don't you...?"
Tadokoro felt sorry for the former player's spirit.
He must have seen his own situation in the spirit's.
And so he made up his mind.
He would summon the demon.
And once he was captain again, he'd have the whole team hold a memorial for that spirit.{p}

"Thank you, Tadokoro.
Well then, once you've gathered the ingredients, come back here again..."
With that, the former player's spirit vanished.
Tadokoro got everything ready right away.
And then he performed the ritual to summon the demon.{p}
